text:
When a trope name such as 'Darga' or 'Sof Aliyah' is clicked on the main display trope table, an info panel will open with detials about the selected trope. Note that all the standard tropes appear in the table as well as some 'synthetic' combination names created for this applicaiton which allow for several standard trope names to be played back in a with a single reference using the combo name.  This is utilized because the note sequence in these playbacks usually contains a variation in melody that departs from the standard, or generic melodies for that note.  Typically this occurs with the melodies used at the end of a selection for a particualar reader's portion.  Thus the combination trope will play all the melodies for this altered section.

 There are several itmes of information on the information panel.

The English name of the trope name appears at the top right of the panel.  The three image boxes in the middel of the panel contain the Hebew speling of the trop name including vowels and the associated cantillation marking.  The middle image is the music staff with the notes used to define the melody with the English tranliteration of the Hebew name appaering as lyics under the staff.  The rightmost image notates the trope symbol attached to a generic place holder represented by a dotted circle.

 For some tropes, such as Munach L'garmeih and Sof Pasuk where addtional markings are found in the text line that define these special cases, that additional mark is also displayed in this box but that mark is not associated with a trope symbol. So a Sof Pasuk will be shown as trailing the final syllable in a line, with a silluq as the actual diacritical trope marking on the word.   So the Sof Pasuk is a trope consists of a diacritical marking, the silluq, and the trailing mark that looks like a colon.

Below these items is a block with a music note symbol which will play the generic trope sound for the trope and is the audio playback of the notes in the music staff line.  At the bottom right of the screen is a symbol that will either be a circled '+' or a circled '-'  that can be used to zoom the image size for this screen up or down for easier reading.  The form is dismissed by clicking the Close button.

 The trope melodies for the generic trope are based on music noted in 'The Art of Torah Cantillation' by Marshall Portnoy and Josee Wolff.  The pitch of the notes and their durations is based on their musiscal setting and interpretion of Avery/Binder trope used by the Reform Movement. In this publication there are 41 lines of music containing multiple repetions of common notes when necessary in various trope combinations.  In creating this application, is was noted that for all tropes other than Muncach,  these musical patterns did not vary from each other other than a possible pitch change in some instances.  Thus these patterns could be presented by a single audio representation.  Any variation was considered too slight to present any significant variation in the perceived playback.   For Munach,  two patterns were noted for all uses other than Munach L'garmeih which was noted to be a separate trope pattern for purposes of this applicaiton
